title: Terraform VPC connectivity blueprint with endpoint health probes
creator: Riley Mendoza
description: Create a single, opinionated Terraform module that provisions a production-ready VPC connectivity stack for Private deployments. The module must support: (1) multi-AZ subnet layout (public, private with NAT, isolated), (2) configurable IGW and managed NAT Gateway or optional NAT Gateway pooling, (3) route tables and explicit route propagation for peering/transit gateways, (4) gateway and interface VPC endpoints for core services (S3, ECR, SSM/SSM Session Manager, Secrets Manager, CloudWatch Logs), (5) endpoint policies and least-privilege defaults, (6) automated endpoint health probing (Route53 or Lambda-based probes) and remediation hooks, (7) outputs for downstream modules (route table IDs, endpoint IDs, NAT metrics), and (8) upgrade/versioning strategy for state migrations and in-place changes. The module should be safe for customer Private deployments (non-destructive defaults), include CI-driven TF plan checks, and a small integration test that runs in a sandbox account. Emphasize clear knobs for enterprise customers: restrict public IP assignment, enable/disable endpoints, choose NAT topology, and pin az-specific subnet CIDRs. Document limitations, breakage windows for rolling upgrades, and recommended rollback steps.
acceptance_criteria: Terraform module 'redwood_vpc_connectivity' created under modules/networking with documented inputs/outputs
Module can deploy a 3-AZ VPC with public/private/isolated subnets and attach IGW + NAT Gateways via a single apply in CI sandbox
Configurable provisioner to create S3, ECR, Secrets Manager endpoints as interface or gateway types with endpoint policies applied
Endpoint health probe runs every minute (configurable) and writes status to CloudWatch; failing endpoint triggers a configurable remediation hook (SNS/Lambda)
Upgrade guide included: steps to add/remove endpoints, replace NAT topology, and perform route table rotations without service downtime
TF plan guardrails in CI block any destructive change to core CIDR or public subnet allocation unless explicit override flag is set
Module exposes outputs: vpc_id, public_subnet_ids, private_subnet_ids, isolated_subnet_ids, route_table_ids, nat_gateway_ids, endpoint_ids
Integration test and a sample usage example exist in examples/ with preflight checks and documented cost estimates
tasks: Design module API and input defaults (owner: Aisha)
Implement core resources: aws_vpc, aws_subnet, aws_internet_gateway, aws_route_table, aws_route
Implement NAT options: managed aws_nat_gateway with autoscaled create_count OR single NAT per AZ (decide in review)
Implement VPC endpoints: s3 (gateway) + configurable interface endpoints list with optional policy attachment
Build endpoint health probe Lambda + CloudWatch metric + simple remediation SNS topic
Write CI TF plan checks and a sandbox integration workflow (github actions)
Author upgrade and rollback documentation + example migration scenarios
Write unit/acceptance tests for TF module and run in sandbox account
